summary: Stone lookout house on Lake Mountain above Hamburg, Klamath NF, built 1912; topped by a CCC-built 14x14 R-1 cab in 1933; wrapped against fire in 2014 and 2025 and still in service.

facts.design: stone groundhouse (1912) with a 14 x 14 ft R-1 wooden hip-roofed cab and catwalk added in 1933; two stories, the stone house forming the first floor

staffing.status: in continuous operation; long-time lookout Nancy Hood named in the register; described in 2025 as part of the wildfire detection network

access.note: Active Klamath National Forest lookout. A 2012 centennial event limited parking to 16 vehicles and used a shuttle two miles from the lookout. No source says the public may visit at other times.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Klamath National Forest

events.note: James Clyman named as the lookout man stationed on Lake Mountain above Hamburg. The August 31, 1911 clipping plans a permanent stone building about 12 x 14 ft, and a July 13, 1911 clipping shows a lookout station already reporting fires.
Register gives 1912. A June 1912 clipping says a small stone house was erected and roofed with corrugated iron.
Clyman spotted a fire on Horse Creek (clipping of September 5, 1912) that was undoubtedly incendiary and burned over 600 acres.
Lightning struck the lookout house near Hamburg and cut the telephone line (clipping of August 7, 1913).
William Hicks named as lookout on Lake Mountain.
Will Hicks described as look-out man for the government.

Register: stone roof modified in 1933 with a 14 x 14 ft R-1 wooden hip-roofed cab and catwalk. Clippings say a new standard lookout house was completed in October 1933 (clipping of October 31, 1933), and a Blue Lake Advocate item of November 4, 1933 reports it was built with CCC labor.
Civilian Conservation Corps crew built the cab and the Lake Mountain Trail to the summit.
Date registered January 26, 1996; US 159, CA 6; nominated by James Rock and Candice Cook, USFS, Klamath NF Yreka.
Happy Camp Complex threatened the lookout. It was wrapped in flame retardant foil.
Long-time lookout Nancy Hood lost her home to the Happy Camp Complex on September 8, 2014, according to a clipping.
During the Blue Fire, crews worked to unwrap the protected lookout. Release dated September 17, 2025.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An August 1911 clipping planned a stone building about 12 x 14 ft. The register gives the original stone groundhouse as 15 x 15 ft. The sources do not explain the difference, so the story says the early size is not settled.

The register lists the Oak Knoll Ranger District as a cooperator. The 1933 clipping names the Scott River District and the 2012 flyer names the Salmon/Scott River Ranger District. The sources do not explain the change, so the record does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1912 build date and 1996 registration confirmed on the NHLR page. Brief's 2070.2 m elevation matches the NHLR's 6,792 ft (2,070 m). Brief's height_m 9.1 is not supported by any page read in this pass, so it is left out of facts; the editor should check it against the NHLR or the flyer. The 'two_story' kind is supported by the NHLR photo caption about the 1912 house forming the first floor. Access 'restricted' is a judgment: the 2025 release calls it an active part of the detection network and the 2012 event used limited parking. The 2014 and 2025 fire items come from a Forest Lookouts page and a republished Forest Service release. Current staffing is not confirmed beyond the release's wording. The flyer PDF was read directly. Not verified: the NHLR's 'Oak Knoll' cooperator versus the Scott River and Salmon/Scott district names. No photos added: the NHLR photo credits (Ron Kemnow, Nancy Hood Collection) have no licence stated in what was read.
